# prompt-weight: what is lost when instruction text is taken away

## 1. Hypothesis

Much of the control's instructions does no work: the model would behave the same without it, or it repeats or
contradicts another sentence. A much smaller prompt should then lose little, and what it does lose shows which
sentences are needed.

**Result in one line:** half right. Repetition and conflict cost nothing measurable and can go. But four or five
sentences are doing real work, and none of the three prompts gets `outdoor-fitting` sliced, because that failure
comes from refused tool calls and not from the amount of text.

## 2. The arms

Control: `exp\control-instructions.txt`, 3,441 characters, 526 words. Both arms replace the whole text.

**`bare`** (351 characters, 10% of the control):

```
You are JusPrin, the 3D printing app. In app-generated messages, OrcaSlicer also refers to this same app. You act on the open project by calling the app's tools. Never claim a change succeeded until a function_call_output says it did. Use only IDs from the current workspace context or tool results. A question does not authorize changing the project.
```

**`once`** (2,616 characters, 76%). Every rule once, tool names kept, conflicts resolved toward the specific
sentence. Stating everything once removed only a quarter of the text: the control is repetitive, but mostly it is
long because it asks for many different things.

```
You are JusPrin, the 3D printing app; app-generated messages also call it OrcaSlicer. Help users answer questions, prepare prints, adjust projects and troubleshoot, speaking in first person about the app's actions. Use only IDs from current workspace context or tool results. Questions and troubleshooting call for answers and recommendations, not project changes or a preparation sequence. Make a requested change by calling its tool. Say it succeeded only after a function_call_output says so (a call that starts an action has not finished it), then briefly report the actual result. A selected filament preset does not prove which spool is loaded: use the physical facts the person gives and ask about consequential unknowns the evidence cannot resolve.

Intent: When the person says what a print is for, or states a requirement, record it with intent_update: the purpose as setupTitle, each requirement as a field. Do this in any turn, questions included; it changes no print setting. Record only what they said: leave out or mark assumed a file name, a selected preset or material, and your own conclusions.

The object: When it matters what an object is and the person has not said, read its shape with object_analyze before you judge (a file name says little) and offer your idea as a guess to confirm.

Setup: When the intended use or a requirement becomes clear or changes, not when it is only restated or a title is recorded, assess the current material, filament preset and process preset against it. Read the effective settings, including customizations and object overrides; preset names alone do not establish suitability. Keep what suits. Otherwise explain why and recommend a material, a compatible preset (presets_list lists the filament and process presets this printer can use) or a focused settings adjustment. Material and saved filament preset are separate decisions, and the material informs process settings.

Preparation: When asked to prepare or print a model, inspect the project, keep what suits and change what does not, so that printer, filament and process fit the print. If that takes several changes, first record the plan and consequential assumptions with plan_set.

Verification: Before reporting a print ready, slice and inspect with slice_report and, when needed, slice_inspect against the user's requirements; revisit settings and recheck as needed, and explain unresolved issues. Check the current slice before exporting G-code or sliced 3MF with export_file. Starting a physical print follows the app's Send preflight and authorization boundary; preparing does not bypass it.
```

## 3. Predictions, as written before the first run

Kept unedited in `PREDICTIONS.md`. In short:

- `bare`: shape read 0 or 1 of 3; purpose recorded 0 of 3 in every scenario; PLA warning 3 of 3; setup kept and
  `petg-question` unchanged 3 of 3; slice read before "ready" 0 or 1 of 3; **`outdoor-fitting` sliced in 1 of 3 or
  more, refused calls several-fold fewer (under 8), failed turns 2 of 12 or fewer**, input tokens about half.
- `once`: no outcome moves by a large amount; refused calls and failed turns unchanged.

The part in bold was wrong, and the reason is the most useful thing `bare` showed (section 5).

## 4. Results

Control is `shared-control\control`, run in the same hours. Counts are out of 3 unless a total is shown.

| Outcome | Control | `bare` | `once` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `what-is-this`: read the shape before guessing | 3 | **0** | 3 |
| `what-is-this`: recorded the stated purpose | 3 | **0** | 3 |
| `what-is-this`: project unchanged | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| `outdoor-fitting`: nothing invented on turn one | 2 (one title built from the file name) | 3 (recorded nothing) | 3 |
| `outdoor-fitting`: asked what the print is for before preparing | 3 | **0** (one sliced the PLA setup at once) | 3 |
| `outdoor-fitting`: recorded the stated purpose | 2 | **0** | 2 |
| `outdoor-fitting`: said PLA does not suit, with a reason | 2 | 3 (one with no reason) | 2 |
| `outdoor-fitting`: ended on a PETG filament | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `outdoor-fitting`: ended sliced on that filament | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `outdoor-fitting`: last turn ended on a third refused call | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| `desk-ornament`: setup kept | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| `desk-ornament`: recorded the purpose | 3 | 1 | 3 |
| `desk-ornament`: ended sliced | 3 | 2 | 2 |
| `desk-ornament`: read the slice after slicing, before saying ready | 3 | **0** | 1 |
| `petg-question`: presets and settings unchanged, no slice | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| `petg-question`: gave an answer | 3 | 2 | 2 |
| Runs with a failed turn | 3 of 12 | 4 of 12 | 6 of 12 |
| Refused calls | 25 | 15 | 25 |
| ... on deferred tools, for wrong arguments | 20 | **0** | 24 |
| ... `settings_search`, looking for a filament | 1 | **13** | 0 |
| ... tool names that do not exist | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| Runs that used tool search at all | 12 of 12 | 5 of 12 | 12 of 12 |
| Requests | 142 | 122 | 116 |
| Input tokens | 1,048,234 | 668,461 | 805,274 |

Refused by tool. Control: `intent_update` 10, `presets_list` 4, `plan_set` 3, `object_analyze` 2, three invented
names, and one each of `settings_search`, `settings_get`, `slice_inspect`. `bare`: `settings_search` 13,
`printer_setup_apply` 1, `settings_patch` 1. `once`: `intent_update` 12, `presets_list` 4, `plan_set` 2,
`slice_report` 2, `slice_inspect` 2, `object_analyze` 2, `preset_select` 1.

## 5. What each behaviour needed

**Survived in `bare`: the prompt is not needed for it.**

- The printing knowledge. `bare` `outdoor-fitting-3`: "PLA softens and degrades in direct sunlight/UV and isn't
  ideal for continuous outdoor use. A better choice would be **PETG**". All three `what-is-this` runs also
  cautioned against PLA for a pressure part, unprompted.
- Keeping a setup that suits (3 of 3), and leaving the project alone on a question (6 of 6).
- Reading the real settings before advising. Every `bare` advice turn called `settings_get` and quoted actual
  values ("Wall loops 2 ... Recommend 4-5").
- Saying a guess is a guess: "Judging by the name" in 3 of 3. It asked the person to confirm in only 1 of 3.
- No false claim of success appeared in any arm, with one statement of that rule or three.

**Disappeared in `bare`, back in `once`: the sentence is needed, its repetition is not.**

- *Read the shape with `object_analyze`*: 3, 0, 3. `bare` guessed from the file name and size every time.
- *Record what the print is for with `intent_update`*: 8 of 9, 1 of 9, 8 of 9 across the three scenarios. The one
  `bare` run that recorded it found the tool by searching after `workspace_inspect` showed an intent section.
- *Ask about unknowns before preparing*: on "I want to print this on my X1 Carbon", control and `once` asked what
  it is for in 6 of 6; `bare` offered to slice (2) or sliced the PLA setup immediately (1) and said "ready to go".
- *Read the slice before reporting readiness*: 3, 0, 1. `bare` reported from the slice call's own result.
- *`presets_list` lists the presets*: without it `bare` used `settings_search` to look for a filament (13
  refusals, one `petg-question` that never answered) and named presets from memory: "Bambu PETG Basic @BBL X1C",
  "Generic PETG @BBL X1C", neither of which exists here.

**Changed in `once`: nothing I can tie to a sentence.** All tracked outcomes are within one run of the control
except "read the slice" on `desk-ornament` (3 against 1) and failed turns (3 against 6). Both come from two
`desk-ornament` runs that hit a third refused call, on tools the control names in the same words (`slice_report`
with `revision`, `slice_inspect` with no `view`). The same control text scored 1 of 3 on this row earlier today
(`earlier\rewrite`), so this is inside the control's own spread. The three-way "do not invent" rule, the doubled
scope rule and the doubled "call the tool" rule each went to one statement with no loss: nothing was invented on
turn one (3 of 3) and `petg-question` stayed unchanged (3 of 3).

**The failure no arm touched.** `outdoor-fitting` ended on a third refused call in 9 of 9 runs. The two prompts
that name tools produce one kind of refusal, and the prompt that names none produces another:

- Control and `once` call a tool they know only by name, with guessed parameters. `once` `outdoor-fitting-1`:
  three `intent_update` calls with `fields: [{"name": ..., "value": ...}]`, turn over, nothing recorded.
- `bare` never guesses a deferred tool's parameters (0 such refusals against 20 and 24), because it only reaches
  those tools through a search that returns them. But it searched in only 5 of 12 runs, and only once it had
  decided to act ("Let me find the slice tool"). To look something up it stayed with the three loaded tools and
  bent `settings_search` to the job: `{"query": "PETG", "scope": "filament"}`, refused 13 times.

So with no tool names the model does not explore; it works with what it can see. A name in the instructions is
what gets a deferred tool used, and a name without parameters is what gets it refused.

## 6. Verdict

The suspicion that the prompt is too complicated is not what these journeys show. Cutting it to a tenth lost five
behaviours the product wants and fixed nothing; cutting the repetition lost nothing and fixed nothing. The text is
not the cause of the edge-case failures here. The cause is that it points at tools whose parameters the model
cannot see.

Wording I would keep: the `once` text. It is a safe replacement, a quarter shorter, with one statement per rule.
Within it, the sentences shown to be needed are the first sentence of Intent, The object, "ask about consequential
unknowns", the `presets_list` clause and the first sentence of Verification. Shown not to be needed on these
journeys: the role sentence, first person, "call the matching tool", the assess, read-settings, keep and recommend
sentences of Setup (the model did all four unasked), and every repeat.

## 7. Cost and caveats

`bare` 668,461 input and 39,102 output tokens; `once` 805,274 and 43,755. Total 1,473,735 input, 82,857 output,
about **$0.15** at list price.

- The instructions are a small part of a request: a first request is 4,214 tokens with the control and 3,630 with
  `bare`. `bare`'s lower total comes from doing less, not from being shorter.
- Three runs, one batch. The control's own spread on `desk-ornament` is as large as the `once` difference.
- `outdoor-fitting` hits the refusal limit in every arm, so its PETG and sliced rows cannot separate the arms.
- Untested, not shown unneeded: export, Send, object overrides, "do not repeat an assessment", plan recording
  (no tracked outcome depends on a plan), and the spool-versus-preset rule (control and `once` asked what is
  loaded in 3 of 6 `outdoor-fitting` runs, `bare` in 0 of 3; too few to call).
- `once` edits many sentences at once, so a loss could not have been pinned on one of them. None appeared.

## Inventory of the control, sentence by sentence

Result column: **needed** = gone in `bare`, back in `once`; **not needed** = survived in `bare`; **kept** = also
in `bare`, so not tested; **untested** = the journeys never reach it.

| # | Sentence (shortened) | Says again / pulls against | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | You are JusPrin, the 3D printing app. | | kept |
| 2 | OrcaSlicer also refers to this same app. | | kept |
| 3 | Help users answer questions, prepare prints, adjust, troubleshoot. | | not needed |
| 4 | Follow the requested scope; questions do not authorize changes or a full preparation sequence. | said again by 28; pulls against 13 and 18 | kept (short form) |
| 5 | Speak in first person about the app's actions. | | not needed |
| 6 | Use only IDs from workspace context or tool results. | | kept |
| 7 | A selected filament preset does not prove which spool is loaded. | said again by 14 and 26 | too few to call |
| 8 | Never claim a change succeeded until a function_call_output says so. | first of three: 8, 9, 11 (31 is the slicing case) | kept |
| 9 | An action starting is not evidence that it finished. | second statement of 8 | not needed |
| 10 | When asked to make a supported change, call the matching tool. | said again by 30 | not needed |
| 11 | After its result, briefly explain the actual result. | third statement of 8 | not needed |
| 12 | Record purpose and requirements with intent_update (setupTitle, fields). | repeats the tool's own description | **needed** |
| 13 | Do this in any turn, including one that only asks a question. | exception to 4 and 28 | needed with 12 |
| 14 | Record their words, not your inferences; leave out or mark assumed. | overlaps 7 | one statement is enough |
| 15 | When nothing has been stated, there is nothing to record. | restates 14 | not needed |
| 16 | Read the shape with object_analyze before you judge. | | **needed** |
| 17 | Offer it as a guess for the person to confirm. | | half: guess marked unasked, confirmation asked 1 of 3 |
| 18 | When use or requirements become clear or change, assess material, filament and process. | said again by 25 and 27; pulls against 4 and 24 | not needed |
| 19 | Read effective settings; preset names alone do not establish suitability. | | not needed |
| 20 | Retain suitable choices and customizations. | pulls against 25 ("establish") | not needed |
| 21 | If they do not fit, explain why and recommend. | "recommend" here, "establish" in 25 | not needed |
| 22 | presets_list lists the filament and process presets. | repeats the tool's own description | **needed**, and a source of blind calls |
| 23 | Choosing a material and its saved filament configuration are distinct decisions. | overlaps 27 | not shown |
| 24 | Do not repeat an assessment because a title was recorded. | a patch on 18 | untested |
| 25 | When asked to prepare, inspect and establish a suitable configuration. | second statement of 18 | not needed |
| 26 | Use known physical facts; ask about consequential unknowns. | overlaps 7 | **needed** (the asking) |
| 27 | Material choice informs filament and process; revisit as constraints emerge. | third "revisit": 18, 27, 32 | not shown |
| 28 | Advice requests call for recommendations, not project changes. | second statement of 4 | not needed |
| 29 | For several changes, record the plan with plan_set first. | pulls against 10 and 30 | gone in `bare`; no outcome depends on it |
| 30 | A clear request for a specific change can use its tools directly. | second statement of 10 | not needed |
| 31 | Slice and inspect with slice_report before reporting readiness. | | **needed** |
| 32 | Revisit settings and recheck the slice; explain unresolved issues. | overlaps 27 | untested |
| 33 | Check the current slice before exporting. | repeats export_file's description | untested |

Counts asked for in the brief: "do not claim success before a result" is said three times in general (8, 9, 11)
and once for slicing (31). "Advice does not authorize changes" is said twice (4, 28), with 13 as a stated
exception. "Make the setup suit the use" is said twice (18, 25) and "revisit" three times (18, 27, 32).

- 4 and 28 against 13: a question authorizes nothing, yet intent is recorded in any turn. Kept 13 as the
  named exception.
- 4 ("no full preparation sequence") against 18 and 19 (assess with read tools whenever the use becomes clear).
  Kept the assessment; the ban now covers changes and preparation only.
- 18 against 24: assess whenever the use becomes clear, but not again. Folded 24 into 18's condition.
- 20 and 21 against 25: keep and recommend, or establish. Preparation now says keep what suits and change what
  does not.
- 10 and 30 against 29: call the tool directly, or plan first. Kept the plan for several changes only.

- **Shown not to be needed on these journeys:** the role sentence, first person, "call the matching tool", every repeat, and the assess, read-settings, keep and recommend sentences of Setup (the model did all four unasked).

## 7. Cost and caveats

`bare` used 668,461 input and 39,102 output tokens; `once` used 805,274 and 43,755. The total is 1,473,735 input and 82,857 output, about **$0.15** at list price.

- **The instructions are a small part of a request.** A first request is 4,214 tokens with the control and 3,630 with `bare`. `bare`'s lower total comes from doing less, not from being shorter.
- **Three runs, one batch.** The control's own spread on `desk-ornament` is as large as the `once` difference.
- **`outdoor-fitting` cannot separate the arms** on its PETG and sliced rows, because it hits the refusal limit in every arm.
- **Untested, not shown unneeded:** export, Send, object overrides, "do not repeat an assessment", and plan recording (no tracked outcome depends on a plan).
- **Spool-versus-preset rule:** control and `once` asked what is loaded in 3 of 6 `outdoor-fitting` runs, `bare` in 0 of 3. That is too few to call.
- **`once` edits many sentences at once,** so a loss could not have been pinned on one of them. None appeared.
